description: Patch releases of Misskey are NOT automerged here. The image's command is `pnpm run migrateandstart`, which is `typeorm migration:run` followed by the server, so a bumped image rewrites the schema of the operator's database on the next restart, unattended and forward-only - nothing ever runs a migration's `down`. A fresh-install Molecule scenario, which is what this repository has, structurally cannot see that risk, and what is on the other side of it is an ActivityPub instance: local posts, follower graphs and a federated identity that cannot be re-created if a migration goes wrong.

The "patch releases carry no migrations" exemption that lets other roles in this fleet automerge does not hold for Misskey. Counting `packages/backend/migration` across eleven consecutive patch spans in six release lines - 2025.10.0 -> .1 -> .2, 2025.11.0 -> .1, 2025.12.0 -> .1 -> .2, 2026.3.0 -> .1 -> .2, and 2026.5.0 -> .1 -> .2 -> .3 -> .4 - ten of them added nothing, and one did: 2025.10.0 -> 2025.10.1 went from 338 migrations to 340, adding RoleBadgesRemoteUsers and unnecessary-null-default, the latter three `ALTER TABLE ... DROP DEFAULT` statements. One in eleven is enough to keep a human on the pull request.

What the Molecule scenario does earn is real signal on the pull request Renovate opens. It installs the bumped image against a Postgres and a Valkey, lets Misskey run its own migrations, creates the instance administrator through Misskey's setup path, posts a note over the API, reads it back, cross-checks the row in Postgres and the note's id on the local timeline inside Valkey, and asserts that the API, the application's package.json, the image tag and the image's org.opencontainers.image.version label all report the version `misskey_version` pins. A bump that breaks startup, the migrations or the API fails there before anyone looks at it.

`versioning=semver` on the annotation in defaults/main.yml is what keeps the noise out of that decision. Of the 985 tags misskey/misskey publishes, strict semver leaves 502 real releases: 432 are `-alpha.N`/`-beta.N`/`-rc.N` prereleases which are skipped as unstable, and 51 are not versions at all - `latest`, `develop`, and the floating `13`, `2023` ... `2026` and `2026.6` tags that move under your feet. Misskey's CalVer also means that a bump of the last component of `YYYY.M.P` is what semver calls a patch, and a new month is a minor.
